content.title: About
content.content: Tomato puree, canned (5806) is a ready‑to‑use product made from ripe tomatoes that are peeled, seeded and packed in airtight cans. The puree has a smooth, uniform texture, bright red color and a characteristic tomato aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes used for puree are often grown in greenhouses, providing a consistent flavor year‑round.
Canning preserves over 90 % of vitamin C and lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Tomato puree is a common base for sauces, soups, stews and pizza.
In some cultures the puree is served on its own, drizzled with olive oil and herbs.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a carotenoid that helps protect cells from oxidative stress and supports heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Tomato puree is a light food suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned puree often contains added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Bisphenol‑A in packaging
items.content: Certain metal cans may have trace amounts of BPA; choose products from reputable manufacturers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tomato puree as a base for sauces, soups, stews, pizza and rice dishes. It can be heated in a pan with a little olive oil, then seasoned with herbs, spices or additional vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the puree in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
